title: code-review-pr-notes-ravi-patel
content:
PR: #1427 -- kv-cache bugfix + small refactor (WIP)
Author: Anika Rao
Context: Fixing stale KV cache invalidation that surfaced under long-running chat sessions + some opportunistic cleanup of cache_manager interface. Targeting a small patch but noticed a couple of broader smells.

Quick summary of changes in PR:
- runtime/python/kv_cache.py: added explicit invalidation on sequence-reset and corrected TTL handling when reuse_prefix=True
- runtime/serving/cache_manager.cpp: small mutex reordering + added ASSERT for cache entry shape
- tests/test_kv_cache.py: added unit tests for TTL+reset scenarios (still missing edge cases)
- docs/cache-behavior.md: draft docs about semantics (lightly edited)

Primary things I validated locally:
- Ran unit tests: test_kv_cache (passes 18/21 locally, 3 intermittent failures reproducible)
- Simple integration run with local serving binary + python harness: observed reduced stale reads but saw a race when two requests reset same prefix concurrently (couldn't reproduce deterministically)

Review checklist (what I looked for):
- Correctness: logic for invalidation + TTL updates
- Thread-safety: locking guarantees across C++/Python boundary
- API/backwards-compat: no behavioral changes for existing callers unless explicitly documented
- Tests: coverage for new behavior + flaky case handling
- Perf regressions: microbench smoke runs

Notes / issues found
1) TTL update path (kv_cache.py L120-L145):
   - When reuse_prefix=True and cached_entry.ttl is None, new code sets ttl = incoming_ttl, but doesn't guard if incoming_ttl=0 (meaning disabled). Need explicit check ("if incoming_ttl is None or incoming_ttl == 0 -> treat as no-ttl")
   - Suggest adding a unit test for incoming_ttl=0 and reuse_prefix True/False

2) Invalidation + concurrent reset race:
   - cache_manager.cpp reorders lock/unlock around notify callbacks. There's a window where notify triggers a Python callback that may call back into cache and attempt to acquire same mutex -> potential deadlock.
   - Proposed fix: don't call Python callbacks while holding the internal C++ mutex; instead, snapshot the entries to notify then release lock and invoke callbacks. This avoids reentrancy.
   - There's a TODO left in code but no comment linking to tests. Add a comment referencing JIRA-RI-7891 and include a short integration test harness that mimics callback reentrancy.

3) Tests: flaky ones (3 failing)
   - test_kv_cache.py::test_ttl_eviction_intermittent -- failure looks like timing sensitivity. Replace sleep-based assertion with event/condition variable or poll-with-timeout.
   - test_kv_cache.py::test_concurrent_reset -- fails under CI on 2/8 runs. Add a deterministic concurrency harness (use threading.Barrier) to ensure the two threads hit reset at same time.

4) Style / API hygiene:
   - kv_cache.py: rename function get_or_set -> get_or_init to better reflect semantics (we set a default only when entry missing, not always). Not urgent but improves readability.
   - cache_manager.cpp: some logging uses fmt::format; prefer LOG_DEBUG/LOG_INFO wrappers for consistency. Minor.

5) Documentation:
   - docs/cache-behavior.md is helpful, but doesn't mention corner-case: reuse_prefix + no-ttl semantics. Add a small table mapping (reuse_prefix, incoming_ttl) -> behavior.

Follow-ups / TODOs before merge (my recommendation):
- [ ] Fix TTL incoming_ttl==0 handling in kv_cache.py (small patch)
- [ ] Add unit tests: incoming_ttl==0, concurrent_reset deterministic harness, callback reentrancy harness
- [ ] Rework cache_manager.cpp notify ordering to avoid calling Python callback under lock OR document clearly with assert/reentrancy guard (prefer former)
- [ ] Replace sleep-based assertions in tests with synchronization primitives
- [ ] Add comment linking code TODO -> JIRA-RI-7891 + add integration smoke test to the PR pipeline for this area
- [ ] Run microbench perf (local): compare baseline for an echo workload (1 token prefix reuse) to ensure patch doesn't regress hot-path (budget: <=5% regression).

Optional / Nice-to-haves (post-merge or next PR):
- Consider adding a thin async API for python callers to avoid blocking on C++ callbacks (might help latency for some paths)
- Refactor cache key normalization into a single util (I saw duplicate code in two places)

Questions for author (to leave as comments in PR):
- Was there a specific workload that triggered this bug in prod? Any pipe to reproduce?
- For incoming_ttl=0: do we treat as "no-ttl" or "immediate-evict"? I think semantics are "no-ttl" but please confirm so tests match expected behavior.
- For notify ordering: any reason callbacks must be invoked under lock? (If yes, we need stronger reentrancy protections).

Suggested review comments (short snippets to drop in PR):
- "Small: handle incoming_ttl == 0 explicitly (see test addition)."
- "Performance: can you run quick microbench and paste numbers? I'll do a run too and compare."
- "Safety: avoid calling Python callbacks while holding internal mutex (risk of deadlock)."

Who should approve / pair-review:
- Primary: Anika Rao (author) -- already assigned
- Secondary: Marcus Li (locking/concurrency expert) -- please double-check C++ reentrancy
- Optional: Sophie Adler (SRE) -- if we introduce any change to eviction semantics that could impact memory usage in prod

My plan next steps (if I take this on):
1) Push small TTL edge-case fix + unit test (30-60m)
2) Add deterministic concurrency test and convert flaky sleeps to barriers (60-90m)
3) Re-run tests locally and push follow-up commit, ping Marcus for C++ review on notify change (30m)

Notes to self: add short snippet for deterministic concurrency test: 
```
barrier = threading.Barrier(2)
def worker():
    barrier.wait()
    cache.reset(prefix)
```
and replace sleeps with barrier and polling with condition variables.

End scratchpad. Will convert to PR comments once tests green and author accepts small TTL change.
